## What the draft contains

- The generator includes a comment client on article pages. `comments-config.js` has an empty endpoint, so the published closed notice remains until a tested endpoint is deliberately configured.
- If configured, the client lists only the endpoint's approved comments, uses text nodes to prevent HTML execution, gathers a display name and comment without email, requires consent, and shows loading, pending, rate-limit, and failure states.
- `.github/commenting/supabase/functions/blog-comments/` is a review draft for a GhostHeart Studio Edge Function. Its public response includes only name, comment, and approval time. New posts are pending by default. A private schema and database-backed per-address rate counter are drafted in `.github/commenting/supabase/blog-comments-schema.review.sql`.

## Security work required before enabling

1. Owner chooses the existing GhostHeart Studio Supabase project for this data, or chooses a separate existing approved host. Never use Axiomara. Confirm database capacity and retention cost.
2. Review and approve the private schema and a least-privilege database connection role. The SQL draft deliberately has no role grants or RLS policies; it cannot be run as a complete migration. Do not use a browser key or a privileged `postgres` connection string for the public function.
3. Verify which ingress header is **overwritten by Supabase's gateway**, not supplied by the visitor. The current official Edge Function and rate-limit documentation does not establish one for this use. Configure `GHOSTHEART_TRUSTED_ADDRESS_HEADER` only after a live gateway spoofing test and provider confirmation. The function fails closed without it. Configure a secret HMAC key and a narrow database URL in Supabase secrets; never put them in GitHub Pages.
4. Add server-side abuse checks and tests for concurrent submissions, malformed content, HTML, spam bursts, repeated failures, cross-origin requests, and moderator approval. Origin checks are a browser control, not sufficient abuse prevention by themselves. Consider CAPTCHA only if needed and approved.
5. Decide who can view the pending queue. The draft intentionally has no public moderation route. A moderator should review the full text, reject private details or threats, and approve using an audited admin path. A tested action must set `status='approved'` and `approved_at=now()` together. The local schema draft includes a decision audit table and trigger, with a unique decision per comment and a policy tied to the resulting comment status. These grants and policies still need a live privilege test. No comments become public automatically.
6. Approve the proposed retention: delete abuse markers after two days, pending/rejected comments after 30 days, and moderator decision metadata after 90 days; approved comments remain until removal. A capped daily SQL job is drafted in `.github/commenting/supabase/retention-job.review.sql`. The POST endpoint closes if the cleanup heartbeat is older than 48 hours. The schedule and contact route need owner decisions before collection starts.
7. Update the public privacy notice at the same time as activation. Draft text: “If you submit a blog comment, GhostHeart stores your chosen display name and comment for moderation. Approved comments appear publicly. A short-lived address-derived marker helps limit abuse; the raw address is not stored in the comment tables. Do not include private or crisis details. Contact GhostHeart to request removal.” Supply a real contact route and exact retention periods before publication.
8. Review the public-function setting in `.github/commenting/supabase/config.review.toml`: Supabase's default JWT gate must be disabled for visitors with no login, which makes all server-side checks essential. Test the live endpoint against staging data, then set the HTTPS Edge Function URL in `assets/journal/comments-config.js`, regenerate the journal, validate the site, and publish as one reviewed release. If the backend fails, the browser shows an error and does not pretend submission succeeded.

Expected API: `GET ?thread=journal:<slug>` returns `{ "comments": [{"name": "…", "body": "…", "published_at": "ISO timestamp"}] }`; `POST` takes `{thread,name,body,consent:true,website:""}` and returns HTTP 202 `{ "status": "pending" }`. Only approved rows appear in GET. HTTP 429 means throttled.

Alternate path if the owner does not want Supabase visitor data: GitHub Discussions with a moderated workflow would require visitors to sign in with GitHub and would send them to GitHub. It cannot meet the same inline, no-login design without additional infrastructure. Do not silently switch to it.

## Verification boundary

`deno test --no-check .github/commenting/supabase/functions/blog-comments/core_test.ts` passed both tests; `deno check .github/commenting/supabase/functions/blog-comments/index.ts`, `node --check assets/journal/comments.js`, `git diff --check`, and `py -3 .github/scripts/validate_site.py` passed. The full site validation covered 63 HTML pages, 254 published files, 401.9 MiB, and zero errors. All four article pages include the gated client and retain the existing closed notice. No endpoint or database test was run.

The repository's site generator currently regenerates unrelated story, navigation, and sitemap output from source that differs from committed pages at this commit. Those generated changes were restored, and only the four article pages were edited for this local prototype. Reconcile the existing generator drift before publishing any generated site change.

## Security review and test matrix

| Boundary | Draft status | Required live verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No accidental activation | Passed: endpoint config is empty and four pages retain the closed notice | Confirm on staging and production after a combined release |
| Pending by default | Pure validation test passed; SQL default and insert both say `pending` | Submit staging data; verify GET excludes it until approval |
| Public data projection | Pure projection test passed; GET query selects only approved name, body, approval time | Review actual JSON and confirm no IDs, address markers, emails, or queue data leak |
| Stored XSS | Client uses `textContent`; comment HTML is not interpreted | Browser test with HTML, script, and encoded payloads after staging deploy |
| Moderator authorization | No public moderation endpoint exists | Approve an audited admin route with a separate identity and least privilege |
| Database privileges | Draft schema has RLS and no grants; endpoint cannot yet connect as a narrow role | Approve/test exact grants and policies in GhostHeart Studio; inspect advisors |
| Cross-origin requests | Exact production origin is required and only it receives CORS headers | Test allowed, missing, and forged Origin; remember Origin is not authentication |
| Submission size | Bounded stream caps body at 4096 bytes; name and body limits are checked | Test chunked oversized requests and malformed UTF-8 at the edge gateway |
| Rate limit | Transactional advisory lock and rolling one-hour DB counter drafted | Verify gateway-overwritten address header, concurrent requests, IP rotation, midnight behavior, and counter cleanup |
| Spam and privacy | Honeypot, no email field, explicit consent, and pending review | Set a real moderator workflow, retention automation, removal contact, and privacy text; assess gateway logs |
| Retention and audit | Bounded delete script, 48-hour fail-closed heartbeat, and status-change audit trigger drafted | Run on an isolated database, verify roles and Cron execution identity, backlog behavior, and audit inserts |

**Open security findings:** The Edge Function must not use an unrestricted database URL or service role; the schema currently has no grant and thus intentionally fails closed. The address header is not yet proven trustworthy, so rate limiting is not approved. Origin and honeypot checks can be forged by non-browser clients. A shared or rotating address can cause false throttling or bypass. The server platform may log connection metadata even though the comment tables store no raw address. The audit trail is role-bound, not tamper-proof against a database owner, and needs a live privilege test. The retention job is drafted but unscheduled and untested; no deletion contact route exists yet. These are activation blockers, not claims that the live site is protected.

## Smallest proposed production change, after approval

Use the existing GhostHeart Studio Supabase project for four private tables and one Edge Function. Create narrowly scoped function, moderator, and retention database roles as drafted in `.github/commenting/supabase/least-privilege.review.sql`; keep the tables outside exposed API schemas. Use owner-controlled moderator access to review pending rows, then approve a specific ID with a single guarded update that sets both `status='approved'` and `approved_at=now()`. Record the moderator role, decision, and time through the audit trigger. Schedule the bounded retention SQL after testing. Deploy the function with its secrets, run the staging cases above, publish the privacy update, and set the config URL in the same site release. No new external service account, subscription, DNS change, or public visitor login is proposed.

**Visitor data proposed:** chosen display name (2–60 characters), comment text (10–1000 characters), article thread ID, submission and consent timestamps, moderation status, and approval time. The endpoint also derives a keyed hash from a trusted connection address and stores that marker with attempt time for up to two days; raw addresses and emails are not written to comment tables. Moderators can see pending text. Public visitors see only approved name, text, and approval date. A moderator role name, decision, and time are retained for 90 days. Supabase gateway logs may separately contain connection data and have plan-dependent retention.

**Capacity assumption, not a price promise:** at 100 article views and one submitted comment per day, the interface would make about 3,030 function calls per month plus retries; comment text would be roughly 30 KB before row/index overhead. Traffic, bots, existing project storage, and the current plan are unknown. Current Supabase pricing lists 500,000 included monthly Edge Function calls and 500 MB database size on Free, with larger included quotas on Pro; this proposal adds no account or subscription, but usage must be checked against the existing GhostHeart Studio project before activation. See [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing) and [Edge Function pricing](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/pricing).

**Exact owner approvals needed:** use GhostHeart Studio for visitor data; accept or change the proposed two-day, 30-day, and 90-day retention periods and supply a real removal contact; authorize the narrowly scoped database roles, RLS policies, audit trigger, Cron job, public-function JWT setting, and Edge Function deployment after review. The gateway address-header proof remains a technical prerequisite even with approval. [Supabase's public-function guidance](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/auth) requires the explicit `verify_jwt = false` choice for anonymous calls.
